have a share in Olam Haba,
except for those listed in Perek Chelek.
And likewise one must examine closely
One who joins Geulah to Tefillah, etc.,"
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba."
And likewise one must examine closely
what they said in the Gemara (Taanis 22a),
and certainly they did not ask
עַל שׁוּק שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
have a share in Olam Haba!
And why did he single out specifically those men,
to the point that he asked him,
In a similar vein Tosafos asked
"destined for the life of Olam Haba,"
and they answered that wherever it says "destined"
it means without judgment and without suffering.
אֲבָל עַל לְשׁוֹן בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא קָשֶׁה.
but with the expression "ben Olam Haba" it is difficult.
כָּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
his dust will not be stirred up,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הָקִיצוּ וְרַנְּנוּ שׁוֹכְנֵי עָפָר וְכוּלֵּי
as it says, 'Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust,' etc."
that one who denies techiyas hameisim,
will have no share in it —
אַךְ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
However, all of Yisrael have a share in Olam Haba
when they arise at techiyas hameisim.
And certainly they will all arise,
except for those listed in the Mishnah of Chelek
and when they arise they will have a share.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ דְּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
And what they said, that one who has arrogance —
that his dust is not stirred up —
is this: "his dust is stirred up"
means that he himself who died,
and remembers all that he went through
As we find in the Gemara, Yerushalmi and Midrashim
that they refer to the death of tzaddikim
with the expression "when he fell asleep,"
and afterward he wakes from his sleep.
"'When you walk, it will lead you' (Mishlei 6:22) —
'when you lie down, it will watch over you' —
'and when you awake, it will speak for you' —
For since death is only like sleep,
afterward, when he wakes from his sleep,
like one who wakes from his sleep
שֶׁזּוֹכֵר מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלָיו קוֹדֶם הַשֵּׁינָה.
and remembers what he went through before sleeping.
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
and did not become a neighbor of the dust in his lifetime —
his dust is not stirred up
so as to be the very self who died;
rather, he will be like a new creation,
וְאֵינֶנּוּ זוֹכֵר כְּלָל מִן הֶעָבָר עָלָיו,
and he does not remember at all what he went through before,
וְגַם תַּלְמוּדוֹ שֶׁלָּמַד כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו
and even the learning he learned all the days of his life
is forgotten, and he is merely like a new creation.
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צב, ב)
So too what we find in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 92b)
about the dead whom Yechezkel revived,
אַף דְּהֵם מִן הַמְּנוּיִין בְּמִשְׁנַת חֵלֶק
Even though they are among those listed in the Mishnah of Chelek
as having no share in Olam Haba,
and in the Gemara it was taught,
לְפִיכָךְ לֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ חֵלֶק בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים —
therefore he will have no share in techiyas hameisim" —
גַּם הֵם לֹא הָיָה נַפְשָׁם נִנְעָר
their souls too were not roused
like one who wakes from sleep.
And although one who denies techiyas hameisim
even then it was not a revival
And this is the meaning of what he said,
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
"He is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba":
just as he is in his lifetime,
כֵּן יִהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
so will he be in the future a ben Olam Haba;
and death will be for him only like sleep,
and he will remember his students
and all that he went through, as was said.
אִיכָּא בְּהַאי שׁוּקָא בַּר עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי.
"Is there in this marketplace a ben Olam Haba?"
which is the voice of Torah.
that is the voice of tefillah, which is avodah,
for "what is the avodah of the heart?
and "they instituted them in place of the tamid offerings"
only that they are men of good deeds
and did kindness for the captive women;
and through it he did good deeds.
who were engaged in gemilus chassadim.
to be a ben Olam Haba.
And we pray at the siyum of a masechta,
"May you not be forgotten from us,
and may we not be forgotten from you,
nor in the World to Come,"
and may there be fulfilled in us
"When you lie down… and when you awake, it will speak for you,"
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רַק כְּמוֹ יְקִיצָה מִשֵּׁינָה לְעָלְמָא,
that it be only like waking from sleep into the next world,
and he will remember his learning.
And this is what it says at the conclusion,
שֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא, כָּאָמוּר:
that he himself is a ben Olam Haba, as was said.
And I heard from our holy Rebbe,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing:
"The beginning of Your word is truth" (Tehillim 119:160) —
whose root is the Aseres HaDibros,
the Mishnah begins with mem: Me'eimasai;
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
This follows what they said in the Midrash
חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֱמֶת.
"The seal of HaKadosh Baruch Hu is emes."
For alef is the head of the letters,
and tav the end of the alef-beis,
עַל שֵׁם אֲנִי רִאשׁוֹן וַאֲנִי אַחֲרוֹן
corresponding to "I am first and I am last"
for it is the Torah that preceded
and it is alef, whose letters spell pele, wonder —
all that was hidden from before the creation of the world;
to know "the way in which he shall walk
and the deed that he shall do,"
"Those whose way is perfect, who walk in the Torah of Hashem."
And likewise, "Your word is a lamp for my feet," etc.
and likewise, "When you walk, it will lead you," etc.
And it begins with mem, Me'eimasai,
the reasons and secrets of Torah, begins with tav.
מֵרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה,
that the letter tav belongs to Olam Haba;
כָּל הַגּוּזְמָאוֹת בְּשִׁשָּׁה סְדָרִים הֵמָּה ש׳
all the exaggerations in Shas are "three hundred"
דְּמִסְפָּר הַגָּדוֹל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא ש׳,
for the great number in this world is three hundred,
while four hundred belongs to Olam Haba,
as it says in the holy Zohar
And for this reason it states in Sefer Yetzirah
that Shabbos was created with the letter tav,
for Shabbos is a semblance of Olam Haba,
and it alludes to the day that is entirely Shabbos,
And a person who is good
מַטְעִימִין אוֹתוֹ מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
is given a taste of the fruit of his deeds in this world
and this is as stated in the Gemara (Berachos 17a),
"May you see your world in your lifetime";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תָבוֹא ד)
and as they said (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Savo 4),
that when HaKadosh Baruch Hu comes
to teach them in Olam Haba,
which parashah he was occupied with;
and he senses in his lifetime
to know the deed that he shall do,
מוּבְטָח שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּחַיָּיו;
is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba in his lifetime;
and this corresponds to "will be," as was said.
And I heard from our holy Rebbe,
that every one of the seed of Yisrael,
in the future at techiyas hameisim,
will be shown not to have died,
but only to have been as one asleep,
"Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust,"
and as it is expounded in the Gemara (Taanis 5b),
just as his seed is alive,
so too it compares his seed to him,
for all the seed of Yaakov will be shown to be
at the level of "Yaakov did not die";
and when he wakes from his sleep
he will remember all the words of Torah.
"May you not be forgotten from us,
nor in the World to Come."
